Framingham Heart Study Cardiovascular Survival Data

Source: R/data.R
frmgham2_survival.Rd

This dataset contains baseline demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, medical history, and follow-up information for participants from the Framingham Heart Study. It is a subset of the Framingham longitudinal teaching dataset, restricted to baseline examination records (period 1), with additional information on the occurrence and timing of cardiovascular events and mortality.

Usage

frmgham2_survival

Format

frmgham2_survival

A data frame with 4,402 rows and 40 columns:

randid

Unique identifier for each participant

sex

Sex of the participant. 1 = male; 2 = female

totchol

Total serum cholesterol level (mg/dL)

age

Age of the participant at examination (years)

sysbp

Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)

diabp

Diastolic blood pressure (mmHg)

cursmoke

Current cigarette smoking status. 0 = no; 1 = yes

cigpday

Number of cigarettes smoked per day

bmi

Body mass index (kg/m^2)

diabetes

Diabetes status. 0 = no; 1 = yes

bpmeds

Use of antihypertensive medication. 0 = no; 1 = yes

heartrte

Resting ventricular heart rate (beats per minute)

glucose

Blood glucose level (mg/dL)

educ

Educational attainment category (1–4)

prevchd

History of coronary heart disease at baseline. 0 = no; 1 = yes

prevap

History of angina pectoris at baseline. 0 = no; 1 = yes

prevmi

History of myocardial infarction at baseline. 0 = no; 1 = yes

prevstrk

History of stroke at baseline. 0 = no; 1 = yes

prevhyp

History of hypertension at baseline. 0 = no; 1 = yes

time

Time since the beginning of the study (days)

period

Examination period. 1 = baseline examination

hdlc

High-density lipoprotein cholesterol (mg/dL)

ldlc

Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (mg/dL)

death

Death during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

angina

Occurrence of angina pectoris during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

hospmi

Hospitalization for myocardial infarction during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

MI_FCHD

Occurrence of myocardial infarction or fatal coronary heart disease during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

anychd

Occurrence of coronary heart disease during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

stroke

Occurrence of stroke during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

cvd

Occurrence of cardiovascular disease during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

hyperten

Occurrence of hypertension during follow-up. 0 = no; 1 = yes

timeap

Time to angina pectoris or end of follow-up (days)

timemi

Time to myocardial infarction or end of follow-up (days)

timemifc

Time to myocardial infarction or fatal coronary heart disease, or end of follow-up (days)

timechd

Time to coronary heart disease or end of follow-up (days)

timestrk

Time to stroke or end of follow-up (days)

timecvd

Time to cardiovascular disease or end of follow-up (days)

timedth

Time to death or end of follow-up (days)

timehyp

Time to hypertension or end of follow-up (days)

stroke_or_death

Composite outcome indicating whether the participant experienced stroke or death. 0 = neither event; 1 = stroke or death

Missing values are present for some clinical measurements, including cholesterol and glucose measurements.

Follow-up times are expressed in days. For participants who did not experience the corresponding event, the follow-up time represents the available observation period and can be used as a censoring time in survival analyses.

Source

National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI). Framingham Heart Study teaching dataset.

Biologic Specimen and Data Repository Information Coordinating Center (BioLINCC): https://biolincc.nhlbi.nih.gov/teaching/

Details

The dataset is intended for cardiovascular epidemiology and survival analysis. It includes information on coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and death, together with follow-up times for these outcomes. The stroke_or_death variable identifies participants who experienced either a stroke or death.

References

Framingham Heart Study. National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. https://www.framinghamheartstudy.org/

Graphics and Statistics for Cardiology: Survival Analysis. Supplementary materials, Heart. https://heart.bmj.com/content/heartjnl/103/5/335/DC5
